title: The Loves of the Lovers of Bassorah

keywords: the loves of the lovers of bassorah
full_text:
In the port city of Bassorah lived a young merchant named Utbah, who fell into sudden poverty through shipwreck and was forced to sell his cherished estate. The greatest sorrow of his heart was parting with his beloved betrothed, Rayya, whose impoverished guardian arranged her marriage to a wealthy emir of Damascus.

Utbah, unable to bear the separation, traveled on foot behind the caravan to Damascus, subsisting on wild roots and sleeping under city walls merely to breathe the air of the city where Rayya resided.

Wandering near the palace of the Governor of Damascus, Utbah recited verses of mournful longing that caught the ear of the Governor, Emir Khalid.
The Governor summoned the ragged youth and asked:
'Who art thou, and what sorrow inspires such sublime poetry?'

Utbah confessed his entire history with complete honesty:
'My lord, I seek no charity or gold. I seek only to know that Rayya is treated with the gentle honor she deserves. If she is happy, my soul can endure any exile.'

Emir Khalid was astonished by love so utterly devoid of selfishness.
He immediately sent for Rayya's wealthy betrothed and presented the case with great dignity. The wealthy merchant, hearing of Utbah's profound fidelity and seeing the true devotion between the lovers, declared:
'By Allah, I will not be the barrier between two hearts joined by heaven. I release her betrothal willingly.'

Governor Khalid then did what only the most magnanimous of rulers could do: he gave Utbah an estate in Damascus, provided a lavish dowry of ten thousand dinars, and presided over the wedding of Utbah and Rayya with full civic honors.

The citizens of Damascus celebrated the event as the Triumph of Pure Hearts, proving that sincere love and royal generosity can transform hopeless tragedy into everlasting joy.
moral: Selfless love that seeks the welfare of the beloved above all desires inspires noble hearts to supreme generosity.
